Records remain harness configuration that git-tool can read for CI and merge authority; they are not owned exclusively by dynaflows.

change.description:
## Problem

The setup skill assumed harness check steps replace a repo's existing checkers. Raidar kept its own checkers as repo controls (correctly), so every agent commit ran both copies, configured separately, and they drifted. Example: Raidar's new `scripts/checks/git_inventory.py` passes Raidar's PYQ checker but fails the harness copy (PYQ101, PYQ220) because the record's `guardrails.python` allowlists were never updated.

## Change

- **Record:** `guardrails.check.repo` maps a `check` step to the list of repo checker files that between them enforce its rule IDs (one step's rules may be split across files). The rails already run those checkers through `checks.commit`, so `omp-guardrails check` leaves the step out. The record fails to load when a step is both in `run` and owned, when `profile-check` is owned, when a listed checker file is not in the repo's file list, or when it keeps settings that only owned steps read (`guardrails.python`, `guardrails.paths`).
- **Strict sections:** an unknown `guardrails.<section>` or a non-object value now fails `profile-check`.
- **Setup skill, Steps 0-7:** the repo's checkers come first. Step 1 maps each to the step it covers and how it lists files; Step 3's shadow run compares the harness step with `checks.commit` to find weaker repo checkers; a gap is a repo PR that expands the checker, never a harness step beside it; Step 6 never removes a repo-owned checker; Step 7 runs its own tests.
- **Rails:** when harness checks fail after `checks.commit` passed, the block message routes the agent to adopt mode instead of reshaping repo code to the harness copy.
- **Setting up from any starting point:** project setup names greenfield, adopt (with or without a record) and extend. A repo checker covers a step only with source evidence for every rule ID the step reports; a clean shadow run is not coverage. Both tiers adopt covered steps, the proposal file lives in the draft record, and identical tiers get one approve/revise question.
- No new command and no new `init` flag: `init --settings` already writes `guardrails.check.repo`.

Unchanged: rails order (pathCheck, `checks.commit`, harness checks), whole-repo scope, no baselines, records outside the repo.

## Grow repo controls; harness only for what needs omp

- **Design directive:** `agent/skills/omp-dyna-workflows/AGENTS.md` records the dynaflows principles every change follows (repo independence, grow repo controls, harness-side config, required means required, whole-repo blocking, events to checks, outcome-test proofs, deterministic first, no code versioning).
- **Three outcomes per check step:** `repo` (repo checkers enforce every rule ID, no baseline), `grow` (the repo can hold the rules: a repo PR adds missing rules or clears a baseline in the repo's own checkers), `harness` (needs omp, or no capability yet). No harness step ever runs beside a repo checker, and there is no "owner declines the PR, harness runs instead" route. Step 2 item 7 no longer forbids [...truncated]

change.title: feat(dynaflows)!: harness side of the dependency-audit policy
change.description:
## What

The harness side of the owner's approved dependency-audit policy. The repo's own checker runs the audit; the harness defines its contract, protects the exception file, and judges severity.

- **Catalogue** – `SECURITY.dependency-audit` is now a repo-owned rule (`bespoke`, `always`, outcomes `repo` or `grow`, never `harness`). Its contract covers:
  - scope from `git ls-files`, failing closed on unknown lock formats and unlocked manifests
  - whole-repo runs at every commit and CI run
  - one blocking finding per advisory, in an exact line format
  - owner-only dated exceptions, only for advisories with no fix
- **Audit mode removed** – the `toolchain-parity audit` mode is gone (clean cutover). It was a harness copy with a staged-file trigger.
- **Record** – `gate.json` has a new required field, `ownerOnlyPaths` (list, possibly empty). It is strict in both loaders, so existing records fail loudly. `omp-guardrails init` reports it as `required:` and never drafts it.
- **Rails** – rails refuse an agent commit whose staged or unstaged changes touch an owner-only path, whether dynaflows is on or off. Renames count. The refusal tells the agent to restore the path and raise the change to the owner.
- **Setup skill** – Step 1 maps every lock file and manifest to the audit that covers it. Step 2 makes an uncovered one a `grow` fix. Principle 10 gains the "scope derived from the repository" line.
- **Severity judgment** – `judgments/dependency-severity` holds the questions, label guide, 30 cases, labels, scores and thresholds. `workflows.py` adds `dependency_audit_findings` and `triage_advisories`, with a strict line parser, a fixed rubric in code and an owner report. `patterns.md` and SKILL.md stage 4 describe the stop-and-raise flow.

## Finding-line contract

```
SECURITY.dependency-audit lock=<lock-path> ecosystem=<osv-ecosystem> package=<name> version=<exact-locked-version> advisory=<advisory-id> aliases=<id>,<id> fix=<version>,<version>
SECURITY.dependency-audit failure=<unknown-lock-format|manifest-without-lock|exception|auditor> path=<repo-path> reason=<text>
```

## Before merge

Every live record needs `"ownerOnlyPaths"` added (the owner adds it by hand).

## Verification

- `scripts/run-ci-quality-gates.sh --tier ci` passes locally: bun 121 pass, Python 459 OK.

change.description:
## In short

Treat a failed devcontainer bootstrap or dependency install as a retryable infrastructure error when the repository gate has not started. Preserve cached failure results once the gate begins.

- **Why:** While landing #180, Bun failed its package-integrity check before tests. The runner stored a permanent failed-gate result, so normal resubmission could not retry the bootstrap. The owner approved this separate correction on 2026-11-16.
- **Unchanged:** Repository commands, credentials, required contexts, exact-SHA isolation, and the one-slot execution limit remain unchanged. Successful and genuinely failed gate outcomes remain cached. This change does not automatically retry jobs or suppress failures.

## Where to focus review (highest risk first)

| # | Area | Files | Why it is risky |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Phase classification** | `scripts/ci-gate.py` | A failed bootstrap must not become a cached test failure, while a failed test must not become retryable. A marker written immediately before gate execution distinguishes the phases. |
| 2 | **Execution continuity** | `scripts/ci-gate.py` | Separating bootstrap into another container would lose installed dependencies and exported variables. Both phases still execute in the same shell and container; only a temporary control directory is additionally mounted. |
| 3 | **Behavioural evidence** | `tests/test_ci_gate.py` | Container behaviour is exercised through the existing Podman executable fake, not a live container. That adapter now executes the actual shell command while translating its mount paths, so bootstrap exit status and gate-start behaviour are real shell outcomes. |

**Lower risk, skim only:** `readme.md` describes the retryable bootstrap state and the retained execution environment.

## Evidence

- **Focused CI gate behaviours:** All 17 tests passed, including string/array bootstrap failures, infrastructure resubmission, and cached nonzero gate outcomes. Baseline unavailable.
- **Commit gate:** Passed the normal repository commit checks on the completed implementation. Exact-head required CI follows on this PR.

**Not tested:** The changed runner has not yet been deployed to the live NUC. The tests execute the shell boundary through the established container adapter; they do not use gVisor or external package registries.

## After merge

Sync the NUC deploy branch and run `python3 ~/.omp/scripts/device-rollout.py` until every device row is `current` and the command exits zero. The next bootstrap failure can then be resubmitted normally without owner-authorised job-state removal.

## Notes

- The phase marker lives in a temporary job directory outside the repository checkout and is removed after execution. No harness marker or configuration is added to audited repositories.
- This follows #180, whose authorised clean retry passed and whose contract change is already merged.
commits: fix(ci-gate): classify bootstrap failures as retryable errors

## In short

Make Git status the authority for which edited paths reach `pathCheck`, including paths remembered from an earlier failed check. Files that no longer represent repository changes cannot keep a session blocked.

- **Why:** Three input-selection defects let Git internals reach the checker, retained failures after files were restored to HEAD, and included ignored files when another candidate crossed a symbolic link. In the observed game-system session, `.git/info/exclude` blocked handoff after restore even though it was not a repository change to validate.
- **Unchanged:** Gate configuration, checker command and timeout, canonicalisation, escaping-symlink handling, verification-reference requirements, and CI authority remain unchanged.

## Where to focus review (highest risk first)

| # | Area | Files | Why it's risky |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Candidate selection** | `agent/extensions/agent-rails.ts` | A parsing error could omit a changed candidate. NUL-delimited porcelain is parsed without shell quoting, and rename/copy records use their destination while consuming the additional source record. The focused proofs exercise ordinary live paths, not a dedicated rename/copy fixture. |
| 2 | **Fail-closed query** | `agent/extensions/agent-rails.ts` | A failed or killed Git query must block rather than run the checker on everything or silently pass. The error names Git status and preserves its diagnostic; this branch has no new dedicated fault-injection proof. |

change.repository: raidar: lab that tests whether a coding agent plus a workflow beats another on fixed problems: orchestrator, grading and repository checks
change.title: fix(review-surface): make review-surface-test run and pass on main
change.description:
- Makefile: quality-fixture-synthetic passed --project orchestrator with
  --directory orchestrator; uv 0.13 resolves --project against --directory
  (orchestrator/orchestrator) and refused. Both review fixture targets now
  use the repository's `cd orchestrator && $(REPO_RUNTIME_ENV) uv run
  --project .` form.
- Experiments page: since arms became agent x workflow releases, each arm
  id is one agent spec, so grouping by (problem, arm) left every comparison
  group with one row and no best-delivery headline or gap to best. A
  problem family now holds one comparison group of all its arms.
- data-errors spec: fetch() replaces a forged Host header with the URL's
  host, so the DNS-rebinding cases never reached the server's host check.
  They now go out through node:http.
- quality spec: the default primary is solve_rate_solvable reported beside
  raw solve_rate; the fixture's five pairs cannot reach p < 0.05 under the
  exact sign-flip test, so its verdicts are Inconclusive/Insufficient (as
  test_quality_projection pins). Improved/Worse rendering keeps coverage
  through a routed projection, like the errata primary test.

  under uv 0.13.7 (resolver uv@0.13.7) and re-validated on the Docker

  re-keyed to the new manifest; its spec-determinacy audit is unchanged.

  locked Prettier, retiring their Prettier toolchain-debt entries.
- All 12 tracked experiment locks are relocked.
